facts.text: The Roselle Land Improvement Company, formed in 1866, laid out the Village of Roselle on an area the railroad called Mulford Station, a stop named for the many Mulford families who lived there.
On January 19, 1883, Thomas Edison switched on the world's first electric lighting system using overhead wires in Roselle, demonstrating that an entire community could be illuminated by electricity.

The First Presbyterian Church on West 5th Avenue became the first church in the United States lit by electricity as part of Edison's 1883 Roselle demonstration, and only the second in the world after London's City Temple.
Originally part of Linden until 1894, Roselle was settled before the American Revolution; Abraham Clark, a signer of the Declaration of Independence, was a native son.

Roselle incorporated on December 20, 1894, during New Jersey's "Boroughitis" wave, when communities across the state voted to break away from their townships and form independent boroughs, with Roselle splitting from Linden.
